-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Types.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Config.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--[[
	Projectile/Config.luau
	Turns a caller's Projectile.new config into validated settings. Every
	value is treated as untrusted -- configs are assembled from weapon data,
	spell graphs and (in Studio) a client-tunable debug panel -- so NaN,
	+-inf, wrong types and out-of-range numbers are all normalized here, once,
	and nothing downstream has to re-check them.

	Numbers clamp to SafeMath.Limit (1e9) instead of being rejected, so an
	absurd value still behaves predictably; NaN falls back to the default.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

local Config = {}

local DEFAULT_SPEED = 100
local DEFAULT_LIFETIME = 5
local DEFAULT_RESTITUTION = 0.5
local DEFAULT_TURN_RATE = math.rad(120)
local DEFAULT_REACQUIRE_RATE = 0.3
-- Dilated seconds between searches while no target is held; see Homing.
local DEFAULT_ACQUIRE_INTERVAL = 0.1

export type Settings = {
	Origin: Vector3,
	Direction: Vector3,
	Speed: number,
	Acceleration: Types.Acceleration,
	AccelerationDirection: Vector3?,
	MinSpeed: number,
	MaxSpeed: number,
	Gravity: Types.Acceleration,
	Radius: number,
	Lifetime: number,
	MaxRealLifetime: number,
	TimeScale: number,
	Damage: number,
	Source: Types.EntityLike?,
	IgnoreInstances: { Instance }?,
	Filter: ((entity: Types.EntityLike) -> boolean)?,
	Bounces: number,
	Restitution: number,
	Penetration: number,
	MaxPierces: number,
	PierceFalloff: number,
	Homing: Types.Homing?,
	Visualize: boolean,
	VisualRange: number,
	Model: Instance?,
	Visual: Types.VisualSpec?,
	VisualScale: number,
	DestroyDelay: number,
	WaitForParticles: boolean,
	WaitForTrails: boolean,
	ActivateParticlesOnCreate: boolean,
	OnBounce: ((projectile: any, contact: Types.Contact) -> ())?,
	RewindSeconds: number,
}

local function acceleration(value: unknown): Types.Acceleration
	if typeof(value) == "Vector3" then
		return SafeMath.vector(value, Vector3.zero)
	end
	return SafeMath.number(value, 0)
end

local function count(value: unknown): number
	return math.floor(SafeMath.number(value, 0, 0))
end

local function optionalDirection(value: unknown): Vector3?
	if typeof(value) ~= "Vector3" then
		return nil
	end
	local direction = SafeMath.unit(value, Vector3.zero)
	return if direction == Vector3.zero then nil else direction
end

-- Keeps only real Instances; anything else in the list is dropped.
local function instanceList(value: unknown): { Instance }?
	if typeof(value) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	local list: { Instance } = {}
	for _, item in value :: { any } do
		if typeof(item) == "Instance" then
			table.insert(list, item)
		end
	end
	return list
end

local function optionalFunction<T>(value: T?): T?
	return if typeof(value) == "function" then value else nil
end

-- The launch direction: toward TargetPosition when given, else Direction.
-- Degenerate aims (zero, NaN) fall back to +Z rather than producing NaN.
function Config.direction(raw: Types.Config, origin: Vector3): Vector3
	if typeof(raw.TargetPosition) == "Vector3" then
		local target = SafeMath.vector(raw.TargetPosition, origin)
		return SafeMath.direction(target - origin, Vector3.zAxis)
	end
	return SafeMath.unit(raw.Direction, Vector3.zAxis)
end

function Config.normalizeHoming(raw: Types.HomingOptions?): Types.Homing?
	if typeof(raw) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	local target = raw.Target
	if typeof(target) == "Vector3" then
		target = SafeMath.vector(target, Vector3.zero)
	end
	local acquireRadius = raw.AcquireRadius
	return {
		Target = target,
		TargetTag = if typeof(raw.TargetTag) == "string" then raw.TargetTag else nil,
		TargetTags = if typeof(raw.TargetTags) == "table" then raw.TargetTags else nil,
		-- nil keeps its meaning of "unbounded"; NaN is treated as unset.
		AcquireRadius = if typeof(acquireRadius) == "number" and acquireRadius == acquireRadius
			then SafeMath.number(acquireRadius, 0, 0)
			else nil,
		Retarget = raw.Retarget == true,
		ReacquireRate = SafeMath.number(raw.ReacquireRate, DEFAULT_REACQUIRE_RATE, 0),
		AcquireInterval = SafeMath.number(raw.AcquireInterval, DEFAULT_ACQUIRE_INTERVAL, 0),
		Permalock = raw.Permalock == true,
		TurnRate = SafeMath.number(raw.TurnRate, DEFAULT_TURN_RATE, 0),
		Delay = SafeMath.number(raw.Delay, 0, 0),
	}
end

function Config.normalize(raw: Types.Config, defaultMaxRealLifetime: number): Settings
	local origin = SafeMath.vector(raw.Origin, Vector3.zero)
	local minSpeed = SafeMath.number(raw.MinSpeed, 0, 0)
	local visual = raw.Visual
	local model = raw.Model
	return {
		Origin = origin,
		Direction = Config.direction(raw, origin),
		Speed = SafeMath.number(raw.Speed, DEFAULT_SPEED, 0),
		Acceleration = acceleration(raw.Acceleration),
		AccelerationDirection = optionalDirection(raw.AccelerationDirection),
		MinSpeed = minSpeed,
		-- math.huge stays the "no cap" sentinel; a cap below MinSpeed is raised to it.
		MaxSpeed = SafeMath.cap(raw.MaxSpeed, minSpeed),
		Gravity = acceleration(raw.Gravity),
		Radius = SafeMath.number(raw.Radius, 0, 0),
		Lifetime = SafeMath.number(raw.Lifetime, DEFAULT_LIFETIME, 0),
		MaxRealLifetime = SafeMath.number(raw.MaxRealLifetime, defaultMaxRealLifetime, 0),
		TimeScale = SafeMath.number(raw.TimeScale, 1, 0),
		Damage = SafeMath.number(raw.Damage, 0),
		Source = if typeof(raw.Source) == "table" then raw.Source else nil,
		IgnoreInstances = instanceList(raw.IgnoreInstances),
		Filter = optionalFunction(raw.Filter),
		Bounces = count(raw.Bounces),
		Restitution = SafeMath.number(raw.Restitution, DEFAULT_RESTITUTION, 0),
		Penetration = SafeMath.number(raw.Penetration, 0, 0),
		MaxPierces = count(raw.MaxPierces),
		PierceFalloff = SafeMath.number(raw.PierceFalloff, 0, 0, 1),
		Homing = Config.normalizeHoming(raw.Homing),
		Visualize = raw.Visualize == true,
		VisualRange = SafeMath.cap(raw.VisualRange, 0),
		Model = if typeof(model) == "Instance" then model else nil,
		Visual = if typeof(visual) == "table" then visual else nil,
		VisualScale = SafeMath.number(raw.VisualScale, 1, 0.05, 20),
		DestroyDelay = SafeMath.number(raw.DestroyDelay, 0, 0),
		WaitForParticles = raw.WaitForParticles ~= false,
		WaitForTrails = raw.WaitForTrails ~= false,
		ActivateParticlesOnCreate = raw.ActivateParticlesOnCreate == true,
		OnBounce = optionalFunction(raw.OnBounce),
		RewindSeconds = SafeMath.number(raw.RewindSeconds, 0, 0),
	}
end

-- Burst cone half-angle in degrees.
function Config.spread(raw: Types.Config): number
	return SafeMath.number(raw.Spread, 0, 0, 180)
end

return Config

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Config.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Homing.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Homing.luau
	Target acquisition and steering. Homing.update(projectile, dt) runs once
	per substep from init.luau's Step; it only ever changes the projectile's
	HomingTarget, its homing timers, and the direction of its Velocity.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))

local Math = require(script.Parent.Math)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

local Homing = {}

function Homing.targetPosition(target: Types.HomingTarget?): Vector3?
	if target == nil then
		return nil
	end
	if typeof(target) == "Vector3" then
		return target
	end
	if typeof(target) == "Instance" then
		if target:IsA("BasePart") then
			return target.Position
		elseif target:IsA("Model") then
			return target:GetPivot().Position
		end
		return nil
	end
	-- an Entity
	if target.IsDestroyed then
		return nil
	end
	return target:GetPosition()
end

local function isEligible(projectile: State, homing: Types.Homing, entity: Types.EntityLike): boolean
	if entity == projectile.Source or entity.IsDestroyed then
		return false
	end
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	if filter and not filter(entity) then
		return false
	end
	local tags = homing.TargetTags
	if tags then
		for _, tag in tags do
			if entity:HasTag(tag) then
				return true
			end
		end
		return false
	elseif homing.TargetTag then
		return entity:HasTag(homing.TargetTag)
	end
	return true
end

-- Finds the nearest valid homing target: entities matching TargetTag/TargetTags
-- (or ALL entities if neither given), excluding the projectile's own Source and
-- anything its Filter rejects. Uses ChunkManager's spatial index when
-- AcquireRadius is set (the normal case -- every real spawn site sets one), so
-- cost scales with local entity density, not total entity/projectile count; the
-- unbounded case (rare) falls back to a full scan.
function Homing.acquireTarget(projectile: State, homing: Types.Homing, position: Vector3): Types.EntityLike?
	local function eligible(entity: Types.EntityLike): boolean
		return isEligible(projectile, homing, entity)
	end

	local radius = homing.AcquireRadius
	local candidates: { Types.EntityLike }
	local bestDistance = math.huge
	if radius then
		candidates = ChunkManager.GetEntitiesInRadius(position, radius, { Filter = eligible })
		bestDistance = radius
	else
		candidates = {}
		local pool = if homing.TargetTag then Entity.GetTagged(homing.TargetTag) else Entity.GetAll()
		for _, entity in pool do
			if eligible(entity) then
				table.insert(candidates, entity)
			end
		end
	end

	local best: Types.EntityLike? = nil
	for _, entity in candidates do
		local distance = (entity:GetPosition() - position).Magnitude
		if distance <= bestDistance then
			best, bestDistance = entity, distance
		end
	end
	return best
end

function Homing.update(projectile: State, dt: number)
	local homing = projectile.Homing
	if not homing then
		return
	end

	if projectile.HomingDelay > 0 then
		projectile.HomingDelay -= dt
		return
	end

	-- (re)acquire a target when none / auto-targeting
	local target = projectile.HomingTarget
	local targetGone = target == nil or Homing.targetPosition(target) == nil

	if targetGone then
		if homing.AcquireRadius or homing.TargetTag or homing.TargetTags then
			projectile._acquireTimer -= dt
			if projectile._acquireTimer <= 0 then
				-- Jittered so a burst fired on one frame spreads its searches
				-- across frames instead of spiking together forever.
				projectile._acquireTimer = homing.AcquireInterval * (0.5 + math.random())
				target = Homing.acquireTarget(projectile, homing, projectile.Position)
				projectile.HomingTarget = target
			end
		end
	elseif not homing.Permalock and homing.Retarget then
		projectile.ReacquireTimer -= dt
		if projectile.ReacquireTimer <= 0 then
			projectile.ReacquireTimer = homing.ReacquireRate
			-- No `or target` fallback: if nothing is in range anymore, the lock
			-- is genuinely dropped. Homing.Permalock (checked above) is the
			-- explicit opt-in for "never drop a lock due to range."
			target = Homing.acquireTarget(projectile, homing, projectile.Position)
			projectile.HomingTarget = target
		end
	end

	local goal = Homing.targetPosition(target)
	if not goal then
		return
	end
	local speed = projectile.Velocity.Magnitude
	local newDirection = Math.rotateTowards(projectile.Velocity, goal - projectile.Position, homing.TurnRate * dt)
	projectile.Velocity = newDirection * speed
end

return Homing

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Homing.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Math.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Math.luau
	Pure geometry helpers shared by the other Projectile server modules
	(Homing, RewindHit, init). No projectile/entity state, no side effects.
	Finite-number guards live in Shared.SafeMath.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Math = {}

-- Rotate `from` toward `to` by at most `maxAngle` radians; returns a unit vector.
function Math.rotateTowards(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, maxAngle: number): Vector3
	local fromDir = SafeMath.direction(from, Vector3.zAxis)
	local toDir = SafeMath.direction(to, fromDir)
	local dot = math.clamp(fromDir:Dot(toDir), -1, 1)
	local angle = math.acos(dot)
	if angle <= maxAngle or angle < 1e-4 then
		return toDir
	end
	local axis = fromDir:Cross(toDir)
	if axis.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
		-- opposite directions: pick an arbitrary perpendicular axis
		axis = if math.abs(fromDir.Y) < 0.99 then fromDir:Cross(Vector3.yAxis) else fromDir:Cross(Vector3.xAxis)
	end
	return CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis.Unit, maxAngle):VectorToWorldSpace(fromDir)
end

-- Closest point on segment [a,b] to point p, and the distance to it. Used by
-- lag-compensated hit detection to test a rewound entity position against a
-- substep's movement segment.
function Math.closestPointOnSegment(p: Vector3, a: Vector3, b: Vector3): (Vector3, number)
	local ab = b - a
	local lengthSq = ab:Dot(ab)
	local t = if lengthSq > 1e-8 then math.clamp((p - a):Dot(ab) / lengthSq, 0, 1) else 0
	local closest = a + ab * t
	return closest, (p - closest).Magnitude
end

-- How far along the chord from `from` to `from + displacement` the point
-- lies, as a 0..1 fraction (0 for a degenerate chord).
function Math.chordFraction(from: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, point: Vector3): number
	local lengthSq = displacement:Dot(displacement)
	if not (lengthSq >= 1e-10) then
		return 0
	end
	return math.clamp((point - from):Dot(displacement) / lengthSq, 0, 1)
end

-- Uniformly random direction within `spreadDeg` of the unit vector `dir`.
function Math.coneDirection(dir: Vector3, spreadDeg: number): Vector3
	if not (spreadDeg > 0) then
		return dir
	end
	local spread = math.rad(math.min(spreadDeg, 180))
	-- sqrt for an even areal distribution across the cone
	local theta = math.sqrt(math.random()) * spread
	local roll = math.random() * 2 * math.pi
	local up = if math.abs(dir.Y) < 0.99 then Vector3.yAxis else Vector3.xAxis
	local right = dir:Cross(up).Unit
	local realUp = right:Cross(dir).Unit
	-- Rotate rather than offset by tan(theta): tan blows up toward 90 degrees.
	local radial = right * math.cos(roll) + realUp * math.sin(roll)
	return SafeMath.direction(dir * math.cos(theta) + radial * math.sin(theta), dir)
end

return Math

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Math.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Raycast.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Raycast.luau
	Physical ray/capsule movement casts, world/entity hit resolution, and wall
	penetration. The resolvers decide what a contact does and apply its
	immediate effects (OnHit, pierce bookkeeping, reflection, nudging past the
	surface), then return a Types.Verdict; lifecycle -- Destroy(), time
	accounting -- stays with the caller in init.luau.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Replication = require(script.Parent.Replication)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State
type Verdict = Types.Verdict

local Raycast = {}

-- Clearance when stepping just past a surface after a pass-through contact.
local PASS_CLEARANCE = 0.1
-- Clearance off a surface after a bounce.
local BOUNCE_CLEARANCE = 0.05

-- Built once per projectile and cached on it (Source never changes after
-- construction), reused for every raycast that projectile makes -- Roblox
-- re-evaluates FilterDescendantsInstances against the live scene at cast time, so
-- one instance is safe to reuse across many casts/frames; this only removes the
-- allocation churn of rebuilding it every substep, not a correctness change.
-- NOTE: if a future feature needs to grow the exclude list dynamically (e.g.
-- adding pierced entities instead of the current position-nudge approach),
-- mutating `ignore` in place won't take effect -- FilterDescendantsInstances
-- would need reassigning.
function Raycast.buildRayParams(source: Types.EntityLike?, ignoreInstances: { Instance }?): RaycastParams
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	local ignore: { Instance } = {}
	local sourceInstance = source and source.Instance
	if sourceInstance then
		table.insert(ignore, sourceInstance)
	end
	-- Excluded independently of Source: Source only exists once the firing
	-- entity is registered with the Entity system (see PlayerManager.server.luau),
	-- so a shot fired in the window before that registration lands would
	-- otherwise have nothing excluding the shooter's own character from this
	-- raycast -- IgnoreInstances closes that gap without depending on timing.
	if ignoreInstances then
		table.move(ignoreInstances, 1, #ignoreInstances, #ignore + 1, ignore)
	end
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = ignore
	params.IgnoreWater = true
	return params
end

-- Sweeps the projectile's body along `displacement`. Returns the contact as a
-- plain table (see Types.Contact) or nil. Distance is how far the ray -- or
-- the sphere's center -- travelled, which is what the time accounting in
-- init.luau needs; for a Spherecast, Position is the surface point instead.
function Raycast.castMovement(projectile: State, origin: Vector3, displacement: Vector3): Types.Contact?
	local params = projectile._rayParams
	local result
	if projectile.Radius > 0 then
		-- Sweeping a sphere along a line is exactly a capsule: a cylindrical
		-- body of Radius around this segment plus spherical caps at both ends.
		-- Adjacent adaptive substeps share the cap at their common joint, so
		-- curved paths have no wedge-shaped collision gaps.
		result = workspace:Spherecast(origin, projectile.Radius, displacement, params)
	else
		result = workspace:Raycast(origin, displacement, params)
	end
	if not result then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		Position = result.Position,
		Normal = result.Normal,
		Instance = result.Instance,
		Distance = result.Distance,
	}
end

-- Does the chunk containing `position` currently hold any entities? Drives the
-- high/low resolution decision each substep.
function Raycast.chunkHasEntities(position: Vector3): boolean
	local chunk = ChunkManager.GetChunk(position)
	return chunk ~= nil and chunk.EntityCount > 0
end

-- Builds the table passed to every projectile.OnHit listener -- see the
-- "Events" section in init.luau. `entity` is nil for a pure world/wall contact.
function Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact: Types.Contact, entity: Types.EntityLike?, hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox?): Types.HitInfo
	local normal = SafeMath.direction(contact.Normal, Vector3.zAxis)
	return {
		CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(contact.Position, contact.Position + normal),
		Part = contact.Instance,
		Entity = entity,
		Hurtbox = hurtbox,
	}
end

-- Steps the projectile just past `surface` along its direction of travel.
function Raycast.nudgePast(projectile: State, surface: Vector3)
	projectile.Position = surface
		+ SafeMath.direction(projectile.Velocity, Vector3.zAxis) * (projectile.Radius + PASS_CLEARANCE)
end
local nudgePast = Raycast.nudgePast

-- Resolves `entity` being struck at `contact` (by a raycast, or by a
-- lag-compensated rewind check -- see RewindHit). "destroy" means the caller
-- must Destroy(contact, "entity").
function Raycast.resolveEntityHit(
	projectile: State,
	entity: Types.EntityLike,
	contact: Types.Contact,
	hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox?
): Verdict
	if entity == projectile.Source or projectile._ignore[entity] then
		-- can't collide with ourselves or an already-pierced target
		nudgePast(projectile, contact.Position)
		return "pass"
	end
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	if filter and not filter(entity) then
		return "fallthrough"
	end

	projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, hurtbox))
	if projectile.PiercesLeft > 0 then
		projectile.PiercesLeft -= 1
		projectile.DamageMultiplier *= (1 - projectile.PierceFalloff)
		projectile._ignore[entity] = true
		nudgePast(projectile, contact.Position)
		return "pass"
	end
	return "destroy"
end

-- Attempts to punch this projectile through the wall it just hit. Probes a
-- point Penetration studs further along the ray past the entry point, then
-- raycasts BACKWARD from that probe to the entry point, whitelisted to ONLY
-- the part that was just hit:
--  - Hit: the wall's far/exit surface lies between the probe and the entry
--    point, i.e. the wall is thinner than the remaining budget. The wall's
--    actual thickness (not the probe distance) is subtracted, so a thin wall
--    barely dents the budget and a thick one nearly exhausts it.
--  - Nil: the probe point is still INSIDE the wall (Roblox raycasts never hit
--    a part they start inside), so the wall is thicker than the budget.
-- Returns the position just past the exit surface, or nil if blocked.
local function attemptPenetration(projectile: State, contact: Types.Contact): Vector3?
	local instance = contact.Instance
	if not instance then
		return nil
	end

	local direction = SafeMath.direction(projectile.Velocity, Vector3.zAxis)
	local probeOrigin = contact.Position + direction * projectile.Penetration

	local probeParams = RaycastParams.new()
	probeParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include
	probeParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { instance }

	local probeResult = workspace:Raycast(probeOrigin, contact.Position - probeOrigin, probeParams)
	if not probeResult then
		return nil
	end

	local thickness = (probeResult.Position - contact.Position).Magnitude
	projectile.Penetration = math.max(projectile.Penetration - thickness, 0)
	return probeResult.Position + direction * (projectile.Radius + PASS_CLEARANCE)
end

-- Resolves a physical cast contact. Returns the verdict and, for "destroy",
-- the kind to Destroy() with. A bounce queues a one-shot ProjMove correction
-- (Bounced = true) -- the ONLY streaming a non-homing bouncing projectile
-- ever gets; it tells rendering clients to snap instead of tween and to
-- re-baseline their local physics (see ProjectileClient).
function Raycast.resolveHit(projectile: State, contact: Types.Contact): (Verdict, string?)
	local instance = contact.Instance
	local entity: Types.EntityLike? = if instance then Entity.Get(instance) else nil

	if entity then
		-- Head/Body classification is purely analytic: the raycast hits
		-- whatever real rig geometry is physically in the way; we just check
		-- whether that hit POINT falls within HeadRadius of the Head center
		-- (see Entity.luau's "Head + Body hurtboxes" section).
		local hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox = "Body"
		local headPosition = entity:GetHeadPosition()
		if headPosition and (contact.Position - headPosition).Magnitude <= entity.HeadRadius then
			hurtbox = "Head"
		end

		local verdict = Raycast.resolveEntityHit(projectile, entity, contact, hurtbox)
		if verdict == "destroy" then
			return "destroy", "entity"
		elseif verdict ~= "fallthrough" then
			-- (cast: Luau widens the refined literal union back to string)
			return verdict :: Verdict, nil
		end
		-- filtered out: treat like world geometry below
	end

	-- Penetration is tried before bouncing; a wall thicker than the remaining
	-- budget falls through to bounce/destroy as if Penetration were 0.
	if projectile.Penetration > 0 then
		local exitPosition = attemptPenetration(projectile, contact)
		if exitPosition then
			projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
			projectile.Position = exitPosition
			return "pass", nil
		end
	end

	if projectile.BouncesLeft > 0 then
		projectile.BouncesLeft -= 1
		local normal = SafeMath.direction(contact.Normal, Vector3.yAxis)
		local velocity = projectile.Velocity
		projectile.Velocity = (velocity - 2 * velocity:Dot(normal) * normal) * projectile.Restitution
		projectile.Position = contact.Position + normal * (projectile.Radius + BOUNCE_CLEARANCE)
		-- The client must SNAP on a bounce instead of tweening a straight line
		-- from its pre-bounce position, which would visibly cut through the
		-- surface it bounced off. The snap goes out with this frame's ProjMove
		-- batch (see Replication.queueBounce for why it carries the end-of-frame
		-- pose), even if a later substep this same tick destroys the
		-- projectile; ProjHit is only flushed on a later frame, so the snap
		-- always reaches the client first.
		Replication.queueBounce(projectile, contact.Position, normal)
		local onBounce = projectile.OnBounce
		if onBounce then
			task.spawn(onBounce, projectile, contact)
		end
		projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
		return "bounce", nil
	end

	projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
	return "destroy", "world"
end

return Raycast

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Raycast.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Replication.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Replication.luau
	Everything that pushes projectile state from the server to rendering
	clients (see ProjectileClient in ReplicatedStorage.Shared for the
	receiving side, and Shared.ProjectileProtocol for the wire format). The
	server stays authoritative; this module only ever sends -- see the
	top-level Projectile doc comment (init.luau) for the protocol's design.

	Per frame, init.luau's step loop calls, in order:
	 flushHitBatch / flushSpawnBatch  (start of frame, bounded)
	 Step -> updateTimeScale / updateSyncState / queueBounce / queueHit
	 queuePose for every projectile that is homing-synced
	 flushMoveBatch                   (end of frame, bounded round-robin)
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local VisualOffload = require(Shared:WaitForChild("VisualOffload"))
local Protocol = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileProtocol"))

local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

local Channels = Protocol.Channels

local Replication = {}

-- Bounded per-frame work so one client event never grows without bound.
local MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME = 1000
local MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME = 1000
-- Homing poses are round-robined past this; the cursor advances in real frame
-- order and is never reset by dilation, so changing GlobalTimeScale cannot
-- merge staggered cohorts into one spike.
local MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME = 2500

-- When on, prints every ProjSpawn/ProjSync/ProjTimeScale/ProjHit as it is
-- streamed (individually rare enough to log one line each), plus a
-- once-a-second rate summary for ProjMove. Toggled via Projectile.SetDebugSync.
Replication.DebugSync = false

-- One queued, range-limited message payload.
type Entry = {
	Range: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Payload: any,
}

type BounceSnap = {
	Projectile: State,
	Point: Vector3,
	Normal: Vector3,
}

local spawnQueue: { State } = {}
local spawnQueueHead = 1
local hitQueue: { Entry } = {}
local hitQueueHead = 1
local pendingBounces: { BounceSnap } = {} -- flushed with this frame's ProjMove
local poseCandidates: { State } = {} -- homing-synced this frame
local poseCursor = 1
local moveStats = { batches = 0, entries = 0 }

local function playerRoots(): { [Player]: BasePart }
	local roots: { [Player]: BasePart } = {}
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		local character = player.Character
		local root = character and character.PrimaryPart
		if root then
			roots[player] = root
		end
	end
	return roots
end

-- Sends each entry to every player within its Range (everyone when the range
-- is unlimited), as ONE event per recipient no matter how many entries.
local function fanOut(channel: string, entries: { Entry })
	if #entries == 0 then
		return
	end
	local broadcast: { any } = {}
	local perPlayer: { [Player]: { any } } = {}
	local roots: { [Player]: BasePart }? = nil
	for _, entry in entries do
		if entry.Range >= math.huge then
			table.insert(broadcast, entry.Payload)
		else
			roots = roots or playerRoots()
			for player, root in roots :: { [Player]: BasePart } do
				if (root.Position - entry.Position).Magnitude <= entry.Range then
					local list = perPlayer[player]
					if not list then
						list = {}
						perPlayer[player] = list
					end
					table.insert(list, entry.Payload)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	if #broadcast > 0 then
		VisualOffload.Fire(channel, broadcast)
	end
	for player, list in perPlayer do
		VisualOffload.FireClient(player, channel, list)
	end
end

-- Sends one immediate (unbatched) message about `projectile`.
local function streamTo(projectile: State, channel: string, payload: any)
	if not projectile.Visualize then
		return
	end
	-- State changes that happen while a visual is still waiting in the bounded
	-- spawn queue are folded into its eventual spawn snapshot. Sending them
	-- first would create out-of-order client state for visuals not built yet.
	if not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	if projectile.VisualRange >= math.huge then
		VisualOffload.Fire(channel, payload)
		return
	end
	for player, root in playerRoots() do
		if (root.Position - projectile.Position).Magnitude <= projectile.VisualRange then
			VisualOffload.FireClient(player, channel, payload)
		end
	end
end

-- Whether the client can't safely predict this projectile's CONTINUOUS motion
-- on its own right now -- see the module doc comment in init.luau. Only an
-- active homing lock qualifies: a target's position is seen through each
-- observer's own replication lag, so local steering would diverge per client.
-- Bounces are corrected one-shot (queueBounce) and personal/local time scales
-- are replicated as a number (updateTimeScale), so neither forces a stream.
function Replication.isSynced(projectile: State): boolean
	return projectile.HomingTarget ~= nil
end

-- Fields equal to ProjectileClient's defaults are omitted: remote events
-- serialize every key name per entry, so at batch sizes the defaults were most
-- of the spawn bandwidth.
local function spawnPayload(projectile: State): Protocol.SpawnPayload
	local payload: Protocol.SpawnPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
		Lifetime = math.max(projectile.Lifetime - projectile.Age, 0),
		MaxRealLifetime = math.max(projectile.MaxRealLifetime - (os.clock() - projectile._spawnRealTime), 0),
		AccelerationDirection = projectile.AccelerationDirection,
		Model = projectile.Model,
		Visual = projectile.Visual,
	}
	if projectile.Gravity ~= 0 then payload.Gravity = projectile.Gravity end
	if projectile.Acceleration ~= 0 then payload.Acceleration = projectile.Acceleration end
	if projectile.MinSpeed ~= 0 then payload.MinSpeed = projectile.MinSpeed end
	if projectile.MaxSpeed ~= math.huge then payload.MaxSpeed = projectile.MaxSpeed end
	if Replication.isSynced(projectile) then payload.Synced = true end
	if projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale ~= 1 then payload.TimeScale = projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale end
	if projectile.VisualScale ~= 1 then payload.VisualScale = projectile.VisualScale end
	if projectile.DestroyDelay ~= 0 then payload.DestroyDelay = projectile.DestroyDelay end
	if not projectile.WaitForParticles then payload.WaitForParticles = false end
	if not projectile.WaitForTrails then payload.WaitForTrails = false end
	if projectile.ActivateParticlesOnCreate then payload.ActivateParticlesOnCreate = true end
	return payload
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lifecycle messages
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Queues the visual's creation; it spawns from its latest pose when flushed.
function Replication.spawnVisual(projectile: State)
	if not projectile.Visualize then
		return
	end
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] queued ProjSpawn Id={projectile.Id} Synced={Replication.isSynced(projectile)}`)
	end
	table.insert(spawnQueue, projectile)
end

-- Destruction is queued for the same reason creation is: a mass expiry must
-- become a few bounded batch messages, not thousands of individual remote
-- invocations in one frame. A projectile that dies before its queued spawn
-- was streamed needs no hit message because no client visual exists yet.
function Replication.queueHit(projectile: State, info: Types.DestroyInfo)
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjHit Id={projectile.Id} Kind={info.Kind or "fizzle"}`)
	end
	if not projectile.Visualize or not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	local payload: Protocol.HitPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = info.Position,
		Normal = info.Normal,
		Kind = info.Kind,
	}
	table.insert(hitQueue, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = info.Position, Payload = payload })
end

-- Compacts a head-indexed queue once its consumed prefix dominates it.
local function compact<T>(queue: { T }, head: number): ({ T }, number)
	if head > #queue then
		table.clear(queue)
		return queue, 1
	elseif head > 4096 and head > #queue / 2 then
		return table.move(queue, head, #queue, 1, {}), 1
	end
	return queue, head
end

function Replication.flushHitBatch()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	local last = math.min(#hitQueue, hitQueueHead + MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME - 1)
	for index = hitQueueHead, last do
		table.insert(batch, hitQueue[index])
	end
	hitQueue, hitQueueHead = compact(hitQueue, last + 1)
	fanOut(Channels.HitBatch, batch)
end

-- Sends at most MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME new visuals per frame, combined into one
-- RemoteEvent per recipient. Simulation starts immediately on the server;
-- queued visuals spawn from their latest authoritative pose, so batching never
-- rewinds or slows gameplay.
function Replication.flushSpawnBatch()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	local last = math.min(#spawnQueue, spawnQueueHead + MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME - 1)
	for index = spawnQueueHead, last do
		local projectile = spawnQueue[index]
		if not projectile.Dead then
			projectile._spawnStreamed = true
			local payload = spawnPayload(projectile)
			-- The snapshot is the client's sync baseline; keep the transition
			-- check diffing against exactly what was sent.
			projectile._streamedSynced = payload.Synced == true
			table.insert(batch, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload })
		end
	end
	spawnQueue, spawnQueueHead = compact(spawnQueue, last + 1)
	fanOut(Channels.SpawnBatch, batch)
end

function Replication.getQueueStats()
	return {
		VisualSpawnsPerFrame = MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME,
		VisualHitsPerFrame = MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME,
		PendingVisualSpawns = math.max(#spawnQueue - spawnQueueHead + 1, 0),
		PendingVisualHits = math.max(#hitQueue - hitQueueHead + 1, 0),
	}
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- State changes (sent immediately, only when something actually changed)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Tells clients the combined Source.TimeScale * projectile.TimeScale only
-- when it CHANGES -- see the "Local time" section in init.luau. In the common
-- case (nobody touches it after firing) this never fires after spawn.
function Replication.updateTimeScale(projectile: State, combinedScale: number)
	if combinedScale == projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale then
		return
	end
	projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale = combinedScale
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjTimeScale Id={projectile.Id} TimeScale={combinedScale}`)
	end
	local payload: Protocol.TimeScalePayload = { Id = projectile.Id, TimeScale = combinedScale }
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.TimeScale, payload)
end

-- Tells clients only when the homing-sync state actually changed. True
-- switches the client into "trust the continuous ProjMove stream" mode; false
-- switches it back to local physics. The authoritative pose rides on this
-- message: it is sent immediately (mid-step) over the same ordered remote as
-- ProjMove, so a separate end-of-frame pose would arrive after the client had
-- already left synced mode and be discarded -- and the round-robin cap could
-- skip it entirely.
function Replication.updateSyncState(projectile: State)
	local synced = Replication.isSynced(projectile)
	if synced == projectile._streamedSynced then
		return
	end
	projectile._streamedSynced = synced
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjSync Id={projectile.Id} Synced={synced}`)
	end
	local payload: Protocol.SyncPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Synced = synced,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
	}
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.Sync, payload)
end

-- Debug visualization of one movement cast (see Projectile.SetDebugRays).
function Replication.streamRay(projectile: State, from: Vector3, to: Vector3, lowRes: boolean)
	local payload: Protocol.RayPayload = { From = from, To = to, LowRes = lowRes }
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.Ray, payload)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Pose stream (ProjMove)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- One-shot bounce snap (see Raycast.resolveHit). Queued rather than fired so
-- a volley bouncing off one floor costs one event per recipient, not one per
-- projectile. Ordering still holds: this frame's flushMoveBatch sends it, and
-- any ProjHit for the same projectile is flushed at the start of a LATER frame.
-- Only the contact point/normal are captured now; the snapped pose is read at
-- flush time, i.e. the end-of-frame pose, the same time base as ProjSpawn and
-- the homing stream. A mid-frame pose would leave the client behind by the
-- rest of the frame the server kept simulating after the bounce.
function Replication.queueBounce(projectile: State, point: Vector3, normal: Vector3)
	if not projectile.Visualize or not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	table.insert(pendingBounces, { Projectile = projectile, Point = point, Normal = normal })
end

-- Marks a homing-synced projectile as due a pose this frame (see isSynced).
-- Payloads are only built for the round-robin slice actually sent.
function Replication.queuePose(projectile: State)
	if projectile.Visualize and projectile._spawnStreamed and projectile._streamedSynced then
		table.insert(poseCandidates, projectile)
	end
end

local function poseEntry(projectile: State): Entry
	local payload: Protocol.MovePayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
	}
	return { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload }
end

-- Sends this frame's bounce snaps plus a bounded round-robin slice of the
-- queued homing poses, as one ProjMove event per recipient.
function Replication.flushMoveBatch()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	for _, bounce in pendingBounces do
		local projectile = bounce.Projectile
		local payload: Protocol.MovePayload = {
			Id = projectile.Id,
			Position = projectile.Position,
			Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
			Bounced = true,
			Point = bounce.Point,
			Normal = bounce.Normal,
		}
		table.insert(batch, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload })
	end
	table.clear(pendingBounces)

	local candidateCount = #poseCandidates
	if candidateCount > 0 then
		local updateCount = math.min(candidateCount, MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME)
		if poseCursor > candidateCount then
			poseCursor = (poseCursor - 1) % candidateCount + 1
		end
		for offset = 0, updateCount - 1 do
			table.insert(batch, poseEntry(poseCandidates[(poseCursor + offset - 1) % candidateCount + 1]))
		end
		poseCursor = (poseCursor + updateCount - 1) % candidateCount + 1
		table.clear(poseCandidates)
	else
		poseCursor = 1
	end

	if Replication.DebugSync and #batch > 0 then
		moveStats.batches += 1
		moveStats.entries += #batch
	end
	fanOut(Channels.Move, batch)
end

-- Once-a-second ProjMove rate summary (see DebugSync) -- real time, not
-- dilated, so the reporting cadence stays steady even mid-freeze.
task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(1)
		if Replication.DebugSync and moveStats.batches > 0 then
			print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjMove rate: {moveStats.batches} batches/s, {moveStats.entries} projectile-updates/s`)
		end
		moveStats.batches = 0
		moveStats.entries = 0
	end
end)

return Replication

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Replication.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/RewindHit.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/RewindHit.luau
	Lag-compensated ("rewound") entity hit detection -- the authoritative hit
	check for any shot fired with RewindSeconds > 0 (see Shooter.server.luau),
	which in practice is almost every real networked shot.

	RewindHit.check only answers "which entity, if any, does this segment hit
	from the shooter's point of view"; resolving what the hit does (pierce,
	destroy, events) is Raycast.resolveEntityHit's job.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Math = require(script.Parent.Math)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

type Candidate = {
	entity: Types.EntityLike,
	point: Vector3,
	distAlong: number,
	hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox,
}

local RewindHit = {}

-- Reused by every check (the server step is single-threaded, and each check
-- drains it before returning) to avoid per-substep allocation churn.
local candidates: { Candidate } = {}

local function byDistance(a: Candidate, b: Candidate): boolean
	return a.distAlong < b.distAlong
end

-- Lag-compensated entity check for one movement substep. Only meaningful while
-- passing through a chunk that contains entities (see `highRes` in init.luau's
-- Step) and only for shots that carry a positive RewindSeconds. Builds its
-- hurtbox whitelist directly from the (loaded) chunk(s) the segment touches --
-- not a radius sweep -- so a projectile only ever considers entities actually
-- in a loaded chunk it's in, per-shooter-desync.
--
-- Two memoization/deferral choices preserve the exact "nearest in-range entity
-- with a clear LOS to `from`" semantics while cutting redundant work:
--  - The rewind instant (os.clock() - RewindSeconds) is pinned for the whole
--    Step (see init.luau), and each entity's rewound position is memoized in
--    projectile._rewindCache, so an entity rewinds once per frame rather than
--    once per substep.
--  - LOS verification is deferred: in-range candidates are sorted nearest
--    first and LOS-checked in that order, so the raycast count is the rank of
--    the nearest clear candidate rather than every candidate.
-- Returns entity, contact point, surface normal, hurtbox -- or nil.
function RewindHit.check(
	projectile: State,
	from: Vector3,
	to: Vector3
): (Types.EntityLike?, Vector3?, Vector3?, Types.Hurtbox?)
	local whitelist: { [Types.EntityLike]: boolean } = {}
	for _, position in { from, to } do
		local chunk = ChunkManager.GetChunk(position)
		if chunk and ChunkManager.IsChunkActive(chunk) then
			for entity in chunk.Entities do
				whitelist[entity] = true
			end
		end
	end

	-- Each entity is tested against BOTH its rewound Head and Body spheres --
	-- Head is checked first and wins outright if in range (the two spheres
	-- are independent, not required to nest -- see Entity.luau).
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	local cache = projectile._rewindCache
	for entity in whitelist do
		if entity ~= projectile.Source and not projectile._ignore[entity] and (not filter or filter(entity)) then
			local rewound = cache[entity]
			if not rewound then
				rewound = {
					Body = entity:GetBodyPositionAt(projectile._rewindTime),
					Head = entity:GetHeadPositionAt(projectile._rewindTime),
				}
				cache[entity] = rewound
			end

			local head = rewound.Head
			local matchedHead = false
			if head then
				local closest, distance = Math.closestPointOnSegment(head, from, to)
				if distance <= entity.HeadRadius + projectile.Radius then
					local candidate: Candidate = {
						entity = entity,
						point = closest,
						distAlong = (closest - from).Magnitude,
						hurtbox = "Head",
					}
					table.insert(candidates, candidate)
					matchedHead = true
				end
			end
			if not matchedHead then
				local closest, distance = Math.closestPointOnSegment(rewound.Body, from, to)
				if distance <= entity.HitboxRadius + projectile.Radius then
					local candidate: Candidate = {
						entity = entity,
						point = closest,
						distAlong = (closest - from).Magnitude,
						hurtbox = "Body",
					}
					table.insert(candidates, candidate)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	table.sort(candidates, byDistance)

	for _, candidate in candidates do
		-- line-of-sight: real geometry must not block the shot before it would
		-- reach this point, so stale rewound data can never be used to hit
		-- someone through a wall. The hit instance must not belong to the
		-- candidate itself, so a target's own body can't block hitting it.
		local los = workspace:Raycast(from, candidate.point - from, projectile._rayParams)
		local blocked = los ~= nil
			and (los.Position - from).Magnitude < candidate.distAlong - 0.5
			and Entity.Get(los.Instance) ~= candidate.entity
		if not blocked then
			table.clear(candidates)
			return candidate.entity,
				candidate.point,
				SafeMath.direction(from - candidate.point, Vector3.yAxis),
				candidate.hurtbox
		end
	end

	table.clear(candidates)
	return nil, nil, nil, nil
end

return RewindHit

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/RewindHit.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/shared/ProjectileClient/init.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	ProjectileClient (client rendering, purely cosmetic)
	Receives the server-authoritative Projectile system's replication stream
	(see Shared.ProjectileProtocol for the wire format, and
	ServerScriptService.Server.Projectile/Replication.luau for the sending
	side) and renders tracers/impacts. This module never makes a gameplay
	decision -- no hit detection, no damage, no entity access -- it only draws
	what the server tells it happened. All client-side simulation between
	updates is dead-reckoning for smoothness (see Prediction.luau); the
	server's own independent Step is always authoritative, and any visual
	drift is corrected the instant ProjHit snaps the final position.

	Modules:
	 init        message handlers + the bounded per-frame render scheduler
	 Prediction  dead-reckoning physics (mirrors the server Step)
	 VisualModel building, posing, culling and retiring the rendered Instance
	 View        camera frustum test
	 Impact      hit flashes (swappable via SetImpactHandler)
	 DebugRays   ProjRay debug lines

	API:
	 ProjectileClient.EnableClientRendering()          -- call once on the client
	 ProjectileClient.SetImpactHandler(fn(position, normal, model, kind))
	     -- replaces the built-in flash/ring effect; see Impact.luau
]]

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local Shared = script.Parent
local Heartbeat = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Heartbeat"))
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local VisualOffload = require(Shared:WaitForChild("VisualOffload"))
local Protocol = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileProtocol"))

local DebugRays = require(script.DebugRays)
local Impact = require(script.Impact)
local Prediction = require(script.Prediction)
local Types = require(script.Types)
local View = require(script.View)
local VisualModel = require(script.VisualModel)

type Visual = Types.Visual

local Channels = Protocol.Channels

local ProjectileClient = {}

function ProjectileClient.SetImpactHandler(fn: (Vector3, Vector3, Instance?, string?) -> ())
	Impact.SetHandler(fn)
end

-- Matches the server's own default -- used only if a spawn payload is ever
-- missing MaxRealLifetime, which shouldn't normally happen.
local DEFAULT_MAX_REAL_LIFETIME = 60

-- Real (undilated) seconds of no ProjMove update before a SYNCED visual is
-- assumed to have left VisualRange and gets cleaned up -- see the render
-- loop below. Generous on purpose: ProjMove batches normally arrive every
-- server tick, so anything this stale really has stopped, not just lagged.
local SYNCED_VISUAL_STALE_TIMEOUT = 2
-- Hard cap on visible Transform work in one client frame. Exact off-screen
-- trajectories defer prediction until needed; complex ones retain simulation. The
-- persistent round-robin cursor is independent of dilated time, so changing
-- GlobalTimeScale cannot collapse previously staggered cohorts onto one frame.
local MAX_VISUAL_UPDATES_PER_FRAME = 2500
local SMOOTH_RADIUS = 100
local MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES = 500
local SMOOTH_SET_REFRESH_INTERVAL = 0.1 -- real seconds; selection is presentation-only
local DEFAULT_SMOOTH_DURATION = 1 / 60

local clientRendering = false
local visuals: { [number]: Visual } = {}
local deferredVisuals: { [number]: Visual } = {}
local visualCount = 0
local visualOrder: { number } = {} -- append-only between compactions; dead ids are tombstones
local visualCursor = 1
local visualTombstones = 0
-- Sum of global (dilated) dt since rendering began; a visual's
-- lastSimulationTime is a reading of this clock.
local globalSimulationClock = 0
local smoothVisuals: { Visual } = {}
local nextSmoothSetRefresh = 0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Smooth set: the nearest visuals get per-frame interpolation
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function refreshSmoothVisuals(now: number)
	if now < nextSmoothSetRefresh then
		return
	end
	nextSmoothSetRefresh = now + SMOOTH_SET_REFRESH_INTERVAL

	local player = Players.LocalPlayer
	local character = player and player.Character
	local root = character and (character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") or character.PrimaryPart)
	debug.profilebegin("ProjectileClient.RefreshSmoothSet")
	-- Keep only the nearest K candidates in a max-heap, so this never sorts
	-- every nearby visual when only MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES can be selected.
	local heapVisuals: { Visual } = table.create(MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES)
	local heapDistances: { number } = table.create(MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES)
	local heapSize = 0
	local function swap(a: number, b: number)
		heapVisuals[a], heapVisuals[b] = heapVisuals[b], heapVisuals[a]
		heapDistances[a], heapDistances[b] = heapDistances[b], heapDistances[a]
	end
	local function push(visual: Visual, distanceSq: number)
		heapSize += 1
		local index = heapSize
		heapVisuals[index] = visual
		heapDistances[index] = distanceSq
		while index > 1 do
			local parent = index // 2
			if heapDistances[parent] >= distanceSq then
				break
			end
			swap(parent, index)
			index = parent
		end
	end
	local function replaceRoot(visual: Visual, distanceSq: number)
		heapVisuals[1] = visual
		heapDistances[1] = distanceSq
		local index = 1
		while true do
			local left = index * 2
			if left > heapSize then
				break
			end
			local right = left + 1
			local largest = if right <= heapSize and heapDistances[right] > heapDistances[left] then right else left
			if heapDistances[index] >= heapDistances[largest] then
				break
			end
			swap(index, largest)
			index = largest
		end
	end
	if root and root:IsA("BasePart") then
		local rootPosition = root.Position
		local radiusSq = SMOOTH_RADIUS * SMOOTH_RADIUS
		for _, visual in visuals do
			local offset = visual.position - rootPosition
			local distanceSq = offset:Dot(offset)
			if distanceSq <= radiusSq and View.contains(visual.position) then
				if heapSize < MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES then
					push(visual, distanceSq)
				elseif distanceSq < heapDistances[1] then
					replaceRoot(visual, distanceSq)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local selected: { [Visual]: boolean } = {}
	local newSmoothVisuals: { Visual } = table.create(heapSize)
	for index = 1, heapSize do
		local visual = heapVisuals[index]
		selected[visual] = true
		table.insert(newSmoothVisuals, visual)
		if not visual.smoothTransform then
			visual.smoothTransform = true
			visual.lastSmoothStep = now
			visual.lastSmoothTarget = nil
		end
	end
	for _, visual in smoothVisuals do
		if not selected[visual] then
			visual.smoothTransform = false
			visual.lastSmoothStep = nil
			visual.lastSmoothTarget = nil
		end
	end
	smoothVisuals = newSmoothVisuals
	debug.profileend()
end

local function setSmoothTarget(visual: Visual, now: number)
	local previousTarget = visual.lastSmoothTarget
	local duration = if previousTarget
		then math.clamp(now - previousTarget, DEFAULT_SMOOTH_DURATION, 0.1)
		else DEFAULT_SMOOTH_DURATION
	visual.lastSmoothTarget = now
	VisualModel.SetTarget(visual, visual.position, visual.velocity, duration)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Visual lifecycle
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Removes the flying tracer. Impact VFX is played from the ProjHit handler
-- itself, so this fires for real hits AND harmless expiry without ever
-- flashing in mid-air. The bullet DISAPPEARS instantly, but the actual
-- :Destroy() waits out the longest lifetime among the effects that were
-- emitting (or DestroyDelay, whichever is longer) -- see VisualModel.Retire.
local function destroyVisual(id: number)
	local visual = visuals[id]
	if not visual then
		return
	end
	visuals[id] = nil
	deferredVisuals[id] = nil
	visualCount -= 1
	visualTombstones += 1
	VisualModel.Retire(visual, visual.destroyDelay)
end

-- Adopts an authoritative pose as of NOW. Every server pose (spawn, bounce,
-- sync transition) is an end-of-server-frame snapshot, so the next
-- render-loop visit must only integrate time that passes after receipt --
-- not the backlog since this visual's previous round-robin visit, which
-- already happened before the pose was taken.
local function rebaseline(visual: Visual, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3)
	visual.position = position
	visual.velocity = velocity
	visual.simulationDebt = 0
	visual.lastSimulationTime = globalSimulationClock
	visual.deferredPrediction = false
	deferredVisuals[visual.id] = nil
end

local function onSpawn(data: Protocol.SpawnPayload)
	if visuals[data.Id] then
		return
	end
	local model, rig = VisualModel.Build(data)
	local now = os.clock()
	local inView = View.contains(data.Position)
	local visual: Visual = {
		id = data.Id,
		model = model,
		rig = rig,
		destroyDelay = data.DestroyDelay or 0,
		-- See VisualModel.FadeOut -- both default true.
		waitForParticles = data.WaitForParticles ~= false,
		waitForTrails = data.WaitForTrails ~= false,

		position = data.Position,
		velocity = data.Velocity,
		gravity = data.Gravity or 0,
		acceleration = data.Acceleration or 0,
		accelerationDirection = data.AccelerationDirection,
		minSpeed = data.MinSpeed or 0,
		maxSpeed = data.MaxSpeed or math.huge,
		life = data.Lifetime,
		simulationDebt = 0,
		-- Combined Source.TimeScale * projectile.TimeScale; updated live via
		-- ProjTimeScale -- see the "Local time" section of the server module.
		timeScale = data.TimeScale or 1,
		lastSimulationTime = globalSimulationClock,
		deferredPrediction = false,
		synced = data.Synced == true,

		-- Real (undilated) safety-net cap. spawnRealTime is THIS client's own
		-- os.clock() at spawn -- fine, since this only needs to be a generous
		-- backstop, not an exact match to the server's own cap.
		spawnRealTime = now,
		maxRealLifetime = data.MaxRealLifetime or DEFAULT_MAX_REAL_LIFETIME,
		lastUpdate = now,

		lastRenderStep = now,
		inView = inView,
		offscreenSince = if inView then nil else now,
		culled = false,
		effectCullDelay = VisualModel.GetLongestEffectLifetime(model),
		smoothTransform = false,
		transformElapsed = 0,
		transformDuration = 0,
	}
	if data.ActivateParticlesOnCreate then
		VisualModel.ActivateParticles(model)
	end
	visuals[data.Id] = visual
	visualCount += 1
	table.insert(visualOrder, data.Id)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Message handlers
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Fires only when the combined personal/local TimeScale actually changes --
-- not a per-frame stream. The client just needs the number; from here it
-- predicts locally exactly like it already does for chunk/world dilation.
local function onTimeScale(data: Protocol.TimeScalePayload)
	local visual = visuals[data.Id]
	if not visual then
		return
	end
	if not visual.synced then
		-- Settle time already elapsed at the OLD scale first; otherwise the
		-- new scale would be applied retroactively to the whole backlog
		-- since this visual's last round-robin visit.
		local elapsed = globalSimulationClock - visual.lastSimulationTime
		if elapsed > 0 then
			Prediction.simulate(visual, elapsed * visual.timeScale)
		end
		visual.lastSimulationTime = globalSimulationClock
		visual.deferredPrediction = false
		deferredVisuals[visual.id] = nil
	end
	visual.timeScale = data.TimeScale
end

-- Homing lock acquired/dropped -- rare, only on an actual transition, never
-- per-frame. Synced switches the visual into "trust the streamed ProjMove"
-- mode; unsynced switches it back to local physics. Either way the message
-- carries the server's pose at the transition, which is the only correct
-- starting point for local physics after a lock drops.
local function onSync(data: Protocol.SyncPayload)
	local visual = visuals[data.Id]
	if not visual then
		return
	end
	visual.synced = data.Synced
	rebaseline(visual, data.Position, data.Velocity)
	if visual.synced then
		-- Reset the staleness clock right at the transition, so a lastUpdate
		-- left over from before it can't immediately read as stale before the
		-- first real ProjMove arrives.
		visual.lastUpdate = os.clock()
	end
end

-- Batched authoritative pose updates. Two kinds of entries:
--  - Bounced = true: a one-shot bounce correction, applied whether or not
--    the visual is synced (for a non-homing bouncer it is the ONLY update
--    between spawn and impact). Snaps instead of tweening -- a straight
--    tween from the old position would cut through the surface it bounced
--    off -- plays the ricochet flash, and re-baselines local physics.
--  - Otherwise: a continuous homing pose, only sent while the visual is
--    synced (see Replication.isSynced on the server for why).
local function onMove(batch: { Protocol.MovePayload })
	local now = os.clock()
	for _, data in batch do
		local visual = visuals[data.Id]
		if not visual then
			continue
		end
		if data.Bounced then
			visual.lastUpdate = now
			rebaseline(visual, data.Position, data.Velocity)
			if View.contains(data.Position) then
				VisualModel.SuspendTrails(visual)
				VisualModel.Place(visual, data.Position, data.Velocity)
				visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate = now
				Impact.Play(data.Point or data.Position, data.Normal, "bounce")
			end
		elseif visual.synced then
			local duration = math.clamp(now - visual.lastUpdate, 0.03, 0.2)
			visual.lastUpdate = now
			visual.position = data.Position
			visual.velocity = data.Velocity
			if visual.inView and View.contains(data.Position) then
				VisualModel.SetTarget(visual, data.Position, data.Velocity, duration)
			end
		end
	end
end

local function onHit(data: Protocol.HitPayload)
	local visual = visuals[data.Id]
	if visual then
		-- Snap to the server's exact position before destroying, so any
		-- imperceptible mid-flight drift from local simulation never shows at
		-- the one moment it would be visible.
		VisualModel.Place(visual, data.Position, visual.velocity)
		if data.Kind then
			Impact.Play(data.Position, data.Normal, data.Kind)
		end
	end
	destroyVisual(data.Id)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Render scheduler
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Visual came back on screen: place it without drawing a trail across the
-- jump, restore it if it had been fully culled, and resume effects on a
-- later update.
local function reenterView(visual: Visual, now: number)
	VisualModel.SuspendTrails(visual)
	VisualModel.Place(visual, visual.position, visual.velocity)
	visual.culled = false
	visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate = now
	visual.offscreenSince = nil
end

-- Roblox performs draw culling. Keep the rig parented; after the authored
-- effects' grace period we suspend emission and prediction/interpolation work.
local function recoverStalePose(visual: Visual, position: Vector3, now: number)
	local rig = visual.rig
	-- Native culling uses the Instance's last rendered bounds. If a camera turn
	-- exposes those stale bounds while the current trajectory is still outside
	-- view, move them outside too. No scene unparenting/visibility override.
	local model = visual.model
	local renderedPosition = if rig then rig.root.Position
		elseif model:IsA("Model") then model:GetPivot().Position
		elseif model:IsA("BasePart") then model.Position
		else position
	if View.contains(renderedPosition) then
		VisualModel.SuspendTrails(visual)
		VisualModel.Place(visual, position, visual.velocity)
		if not visual.culled then visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate = now end
	end
end

local function updateOffscreen(visual: Visual, now: number)
	local since: number = if visual.inView then now else visual.offscreenSince or now
	visual.offscreenSince = since
	if not visual.culled and now - since >= visual.effectCullDelay then
		VisualModel.SuspendEffects(visual)
		visual.culled = true
	end
	recoverStalePose(visual, visual.position, now)
	-- Targets received before leaving view must not continue tweening later.
	visual.transformFrom = nil
	visual.transformTo = nil
end

local function resumeEffectsIfDue(visual: Visual)
	if visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate then
		VisualModel.ResumeEffects(visual)
		visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate = nil
	end
end

-- A SYNCED visual (actively homing) is posed entirely by ProjMove; this only
-- advances its tween and handles visibility. Returns whether it used
-- transform budget, or nil if it was destroyed.
local function updateSynced(visual: Visual, now: number): boolean?
	local inView = View.contains(visual.position)
	if inView then
		if not visual.inView then
			reenterView(visual, now)
		elseif not visual.smoothTransform then
			resumeEffectsIfDue(visual)
			VisualModel.Step(visual, math.max(now - visual.lastRenderStep, 0))
		end
		visual.lastRenderStep = now
	else
		updateOffscreen(visual, now)
	end
	visual.inView = inView
	-- Left-VisualRange safety net. Deliberately wall-clock, NOT a dilated
	-- countdown: a synced visual can belong to a shooter at ANY personal time
	-- ratio, including exactly 0, so there's no dilated schedule the client
	-- could reconstruct. The server streams every synced projectile's pose
	-- regardless of dt, so lastUpdate keeps refreshing while this client is
	-- in range; once it stops, a real-time timeout cleans the visual up.
	if now - visual.lastUpdate > SYNCED_VISUAL_STALE_TIMEOUT then
		destroyVisual(visual.id)
		return nil
	end
	return inView
end

-- An UNSYNCED visual (the common case -- including a bouncer between
-- bounces) is dead-reckoned by Prediction over all global time accumulated
-- since its previous visit. Returns whether it used transform budget, or nil
-- if it was destroyed.
local function updatePredicted(visual: Visual, elapsedGlobalDt: number, now: number): boolean?
	if not visual.inView and visual.culled and Prediction.canDefer(visual) then
		local dt = elapsedGlobalDt * visual.timeScale
		local projectedPosition = Prediction.projectDeferred(visual, dt)
		if dt < visual.life and not View.contains(projectedPosition) then
			-- Leave the baseline timestamp untouched. Re-entry consumes the whole
			-- interval exactly once; corrections replace that baseline immediately.
			visual.deferredPrediction = true
			deferredVisuals[visual.id] = visual
			recoverStalePose(visual, projectedPosition, now)
			return false
		end
	end
	local alive, moved = Prediction.simulate(visual, elapsedGlobalDt * visual.timeScale)
	visual.lastSimulationTime = globalSimulationClock
	visual.deferredPrediction = false
	deferredVisuals[visual.id] = nil
	local inView = View.contains(visual.position)
	if inView then
		if not visual.inView then
			reenterView(visual, now)
		else
			if moved and visual.smoothTransform then
				setSmoothTarget(visual, now)
			elseif moved then
				VisualModel.Place(visual, visual.position, visual.velocity)
			end
			resumeEffectsIfDue(visual)
		end
		visual.lastRenderStep = now
	else
		updateOffscreen(visual, now)
	end
	visual.inView = inView
	if not alive then
		-- Safety net: normally ProjHit arrives first and removes this entry.
		-- This only fires if it never does (e.g. the projectile left this
		-- client's VisualRange).
		destroyVisual(visual.id)
		return nil
	end
	return inView
end

local function compactVisualOrder()
	local oldOrder = visualOrder
	local oldCount = #oldOrder
	local compacted: { number } = table.create(math.max(oldCount - visualTombstones, 0))
	-- Begin at the next due slot so compaction preserves round-robin fairness.
	for offset = 0, oldCount - 1 do
		local id = oldOrder[(visualCursor + offset - 1) % oldCount + 1]
		if visuals[id] then
			table.insert(compacted, id)
		end
	end
	visualOrder = compacted
	visualCursor = 1
	visualTombstones = 0
end

-- Visits visuals round-robin until MAX_VISUAL_UPDATES_PER_FRAME on-screen
-- transforms have been spent (or every visual was visited once).
local function renderStep(globalDt: number)
	globalSimulationClock += globalDt
	local now = os.clock()
	View.refresh()
	refreshSmoothVisuals(now)

	local slotCount = #visualOrder
	local inspected = 0
	local transformed = 0
	while inspected < slotCount and transformed < MAX_VISUAL_UPDATES_PER_FRAME do
		if visualCursor > slotCount then
			visualCursor = 1
		end
		local id = visualOrder[visualCursor]
		visualCursor += 1
		inspected += 1
		local visual = visuals[id]
		if not visual then
			continue
		end
		local elapsedGlobalDt = math.max(globalSimulationClock - visual.lastSimulationTime, 0)

		-- Real (undilated) backstop mirroring the server's MaxRealLifetime.
		-- Normally ProjHit removes the visual first; this only matters if that
		-- message is missed (e.g. the visual drifted outside VisualRange).
		if now - visual.spawnRealTime >= visual.maxRealLifetime then
			destroyVisual(id)
			continue
		end

		local usedBudget = if visual.synced
			then updateSynced(visual, now)
			else updatePredicted(visual, elapsedGlobalDt, now)
		if usedBudget then
			transformed += 1
		end
	end

	-- Nearby visuals receive presentation-only interpolation every real frame.
	-- Their logical simulation and network snapshots remain in the bounded
	-- scheduler above, so this adds at most MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES transforms.
	for _, visual in smoothVisuals do
		if visual.inView and visuals[visual.id] == visual then
			local resumeAt = visual.resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate
			if resumeAt and resumeAt < now then
				resumeEffectsIfDue(visual)
			end
			VisualModel.Step(visual, math.max(now - (visual.lastSmoothStep or now), 0))
			visual.lastSmoothStep = now
		end
	end

	-- Avoid an ever-growing sparse order array without changing which live
	-- visual is next. This is metadata work only; it performs no transforms.
	if visualTombstones >= 256 and visualTombstones * 4 >= #visualOrder then
		compactVisualOrder()
	end
end

function ProjectileClient.EnableClientRendering()
	if clientRendering or RunService:IsServer() then
		return
	end
	clientRendering = true
	ChunkManager.BeforeTimeScaleChange:Connect(function()
		for _, visual in deferredVisuals do
				Prediction.settleDeferred(visual,
					math.max(globalSimulationClock - visual.lastSimulationTime, 0) * visual.timeScale)
				visual.lastSimulationTime = globalSimulationClock
				visual.deferredPrediction = false
		end
		table.clear(deferredVisuals)
	end)

	VisualOffload.On(Channels.SpawnBatch, function(batch: { Protocol.SpawnPayload })
		debug.profilebegin("ProjectileClient.BuildSpawnBatch")
		for _, data in batch do
			onSpawn(data)
		end
		debug.profileend()
	end)
	VisualOffload.On(Channels.TimeScale, onTimeScale)
	VisualOffload.On(Channels.Sync, onSync)
	VisualOffload.On(Channels.Move, onMove)
	VisualOffload.On(Channels.HitBatch, function(batch: { Protocol.HitPayload })
		for _, data in batch do
			onHit(data)
		end
	end)
	VisualOffload.On(Channels.Ray, function(data: Protocol.RayPayload)
		DebugRays.Draw(data.From, data.To, data.LowRes)
	end)

	View.refresh()
	Heartbeat.Connect(renderStep, { Name = "ProjectileSystem.ClientSimulate", Priority = 5 })
end

function ProjectileClient.GetStats()
	return {
		Visuals = visualCount,
		VisualUpdatesPerFrame = MAX_VISUAL_UPDATES_PER_FRAME,
		SmoothLimit = MAX_SMOOTH_PROJECTILES,
	}
end

return ProjectileClient

-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/ProjectileClient/init.luau

--!strict
--[[
	ProjectileClient/Types.luau
	Shared shapes for the client renderer's modules. No runtime behaviour.
]]

local Protocol = require(script.Parent.Parent:WaitForChild("ProjectileProtocol"))

-- A visual driven by a Motor6D from an invisible anchored root; see
-- VisualModel.Build.
export type Rig = {
	driver: BasePart,
	motor: Motor6D,
	rootOffset: CFrame,
	model: Instance,
	root: BasePart,
	poolKey: string?,
}

-- One rendered projectile. Physics fields mirror the server projectile and
-- are advanced by Prediction; the rest is presentation state.
export type Visual = {
	id: number,
	model: Instance,
	rig: Rig?,
	destroyDelay: number,
	waitForParticles: boolean,
	waitForTrails: boolean,

	-- physics mirror (see Prediction)
	position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3,
	gravity: Protocol.Acceleration,
	acceleration: Protocol.Acceleration,
	accelerationDirection: Vector3?,
	minSpeed: number,
	maxSpeed: number,
	life: number, -- dilated seconds remaining
	simulationDebt: number, -- personal/global seconds carried across visits
	timeScale: number, -- combined Source * projectile TimeScale
	lastSimulationTime: number, -- global simulation clock the pose corresponds to
	deferredPrediction: boolean,
	synced: boolean, -- homing: driven by ProjMove instead of Prediction

	-- lifetime backstops
	spawnRealTime: number,
	maxRealLifetime: number,
	lastUpdate: number, -- os.clock() of the last authoritative pose

	-- presentation
	lastRenderStep: number,
	inView: boolean,
	offscreenSince: number?,
	culled: boolean,
	effectCullDelay: number,
	resumeEffectsOnNextUpdate: number?,
	smoothTransform: boolean,
	lastSmoothStep: number?,
	lastSmoothTarget: number?,
	transformFrom: CFrame?,
	transformTo: CFrame?,
	transformElapsed: number,
	transformDuration: number,
	suspendedTrails: { Trail }?,
	suspendedParticles: { ParticleEmitter }?,
}

-- ModuleScripts must return exactly one non-nil value.
return {}
